course.title: Project Practicum I: Software Engineering
course.description: The objective of this course is to enable students to build a professional software product by applying the Software Development Life Cycle in a group project. Throughout the course, students will learn how to plan and analyze a software project, develop a project timeline and schedule, and prepare professional documents such as the Statement of Work and the Software Requirements Specification. Students will also practice estimating project cost and budget, modeling the system using Unified Modeling Language diagrams, and producing professional design and prototyping outputs such as High Level Design, Low Level Design, Data Flow Diagrams, User Interface and User Experience wireframes, and database schema designs. In addition, students will learn software architecture styles and software design principles, including Solid principles and the four plus one architectural view model. By completing and presenting these deliverables as a team, students will be able to demonstrate professional software planning, documentation, modeling, and design skills that support the development of a complete software solution.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the purpose, phases, and key deliverables of SDLC. LLO2: Compare common SDLC models (Waterfall, Agile) and select a suitable model for a given case.

topics.title: Topic 2: Requirement Gathering Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify stakeholders and categorize requirements (functional vs non-functional). LLO2: Apply elicitation techniques (interview, observation, questionnaire) to collect requirements for a case study. LLO3: Write clear requirements using user stories or SRS-style statements with acceptance criteria. LLO4: Validate and refine requirements to ensure they are complete, consistent, and testable.

topics.title: Topic 3: Analysis and Planning Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyze system needs and define project scope, assumptions, and constraints. LLO2: Conduct feasibility analysis (technical, operational, schedule, economic) for a proposed system. LLO3: Create a basic project plan using WBS and timeline (milestones or sprint plan). LLO4: Develop a risk register with mitigation strategies and monitoring actions.

topics.title: Topic 4: Cost Estimation or Budget Estimation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain software cost estimation concepts and key cost drivers (effort, complexity, risks). LLO2: Produce a basic budget estimate using a chosen technique (top-down/bottom-up, analogy, or story points) including contingency.

topics.title: Topic 5: UML-Unified Modelling Language
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the purpose of UML and when to use structural vs behavioral diagrams. LLO2: Create a Use Case Diagram with actors, system boundary, and use cases from requirements. LLO3: Create an Activity Diagram to represent workflow for a selected use case. LLO4: Create a Sequence Diagram to model interactions for one key scenario. LLO5: Create a Class Diagram (classes, attributes, methods, relationships) for core entities. LLO6: Check model consistency across diagrams (trace requirements → use cases → sequence/class).

topics.title: Topic 6: Design and Prototyping Phase of SDLC
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate low-fidelity vs high-fidelity prototypes and choose an appropriate prototyping approach. LLO2: Apply UI/UX basics (consistency, feedback, simplicity) to design screens for key user flows. LLO3: Build a prototype (paper/Figma) for core features with navigation and states. LLO4: Conduct a simple usability evaluation (task-based test) and collect user feedback. LLO5: Improve the prototype based on feedback and document changes (before/after). LLO6: Present prototype decisions linking UI design to requirements and user needs.

topics.title: Topic 7: Software Design and Software Architecture
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Design a high-level architecture (layered/MVC/client-server) and justify choices using quality attributes (security, performance, maintainability). LLO2: Produce an architecture/design description including components, responsibilities, interfaces, and data flow.

topics.title: Topic 8: Final Project Review and Presentation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Compile a complete project portfolio (requirements, plan, budget, UML, prototype, architecture) with traceability. LLO2: Deliver a professional presentation and respond to Q&A by defending design and estimation decisions with evidence.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
